product_family: AI UX/UI design generation (wireframes, hi-fi screens, design-to-code, Figma plugin)

certifications.name: GDPR (posture, not a certification)
certifications.proof_quote: For users in the European Union, we process personal data in accordance with GDPR requirements. In addition to the rights already mentioned, you have: Right to restrict processing... Right to object... Right to withdraw consent... Right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority

certifications.name: CCPA (California, posture)
certifications.proof_quote: If you are a California resident, you have additional rights under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), including: Right to know what personal information is collected... Right to delete personal information...

certifications.name: SOC 2
certifications.proof_quote: No SOC 2 claim appears on UX Pilot's own site. Their /enterprise page only offers 'Security, SSO, and compliance answers' during a booked demo, with no certification language present. A third-party aggregator (Nudge Security) lists 'SOC 2 Compliant,' but this is not vendor-attested evidence, and the same aggregator lists seven conflicting certifications.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: Not claimed on any uxpilot.ai page. Only surfaced via the Nudge Security aggregator profile, which is not vendor-domain proof.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: Not claimed on uxpilot.ai. Aggregator listing only; no BAA or HIPAA language exists in their published privacy policy or terms.

certifications.name: PCI DSS / FedRAMP / CSA STAR
certifications.proof_quote: Not claimed anywhere on the vendor's own domain. Listed only by the Nudge Security aggregator, which is unreliable here (it marks the vendor compliant with nearly every framework simultaneously).

privacy.ai_training_note: Terms of Service section 13 (Data Usage and AI Training): 'we may use anonymized usage data (such as clicks, navigation patterns, and UX interaction metrics) to improve our Services... We do not train our AI models using your generated designs or any confidential information.' So: model training on your generated designs = NO; anonymized product-usage telemetry = YES (opt-in by use). Note the platform integrates third-party AI/LLM providers for generation, and the privacy policy permits sharing data with service providers and using third-party advertising/tracking cookies.

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: Claimed: 'any information collected through our websites or over the Internet is transmitted using current industry-standard security and/or encryption methods'. No specific cipher/at-rest detail published.

security.name: Breach notification
security.value: Claimed: 'If a security breach causes an unauthorized intrusion into our system that materially affects your Personal Data, then we will notify you as soon as possible'.

security.name: Data retention / deletion
security.value: On account deletion, data deleted or anonymized within 90 days, subject to legal/fraud retention exceptions. Right to erasure, access, rectification, portability honored within 30 days.

security.name: Bug bounty program
security.value: None found. No HackerOne/Bugcrowd presence. Terms actively prohibit users from 'Attempting to probe, scan, or test the vulnerability of our system or network'.

security.name: Penetration testing
security.value: Not disclosed on any vendor page.

security.name: SSO / enterprise auth
security.value: Enterprise tier advertises SSO (uxpilot.ai/enterprise lists 'Security, SSO, and compliance answers' as a demo topic). Aggregator profile lists Okta, Google, and Microsoft login support; not independently confirmed on vendor's own domain.

security.name: Data subprocessors / stack
security.value: Per aggregator profile (not vendor-published): Stripe, Vercel, Firebase, Google Analytics/Workspace/Tag Manager, Crisp. Vendor's own privacy policy confirms use of third-party service providers and advertising partners but does not publish a subprocessor list.

products.name: UX Pilot (web app, individual / Free)
products.data_scope: Free plan: personal non-commercial use only. Collects name, email, IP, usage telemetry. Designs not used for model training.
products.notes: 45 free credits, no card required. 1M+ users claimed.

products.name: UX Pilot Standard / Pro (paid individual)
products.data_scope: Same data handling as free; adds commercial usage license for generated designs. Credits roll over with active subscription.
products.notes: Commercial use rights granted to paid tiers.

products.name: UX Pilot Teams
products.data_scope: Team collaboration; same underlying privacy/AI-training stance. No team-specific DPA published.

products.name: UX Pilot Enterprise
products.data_scope: Security, SSO, and compliance details provided only via booked demo, not published. Likely DPA/SSO available on request but unverified.
products.notes: Sales-led; 'Book a Demo'. No public security/compliance documentation.

products.name: Figma plugin (Nodey AI Design Agent) + API
products.data_scope: Two-way Figma sync and GitHub code export; api.uxpilot.ai endpoint. Privacy policy explicitly covers Figma plugins. Imported Figma components and design systems are processed.
products.notes: Connects to user's Figma and GitHub repositories.

compare.pricing_model: Freemium + subscription (Free with 45 credits, Standard, Pro, Teams, Enterprise sales-led)

flags: No vendor-published trust center or security/compliance page; enterprise security answers are gated behind a sales demo.

A third-party aggregator (Nudge Security) lists SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI, FedRAMP, and CSA STAR as 'Compliant,' but UX Pilot publishes none of these on its own domain; the aggregator claims are unverified marketing-style data, not evidence.
No bug bounty and no disclosed penetration testing; terms explicitly forbid security probing/scanning by users.
Privacy policy permits broad third-party data sharing, targeted advertising cookies, and acquisition of data from third-party/public sources; honors Do-Not-Track is NOT guaranteed.
Generated designs are NOT used for AI model training (good), but anonymized usage telemetry is used and the product relies on external LLM providers for generation.
No published DPA; US-only data residency may not satisfy EU data-localization requirements despite stated GDPR posture.
